key_insight: TEON generalizes layer-wise Muon by modeling network gradients as a structured higher-order tensor and performing tensorized orthonormalization across modes, not just within individual layers. This broader orthogonalization yields provable convergence improvements while remaining practically scalable for LLM pre-training.
problem_solved: Layer-wise orthogonalization (as in Muon) ignores cross-layer and multi-mode correlations in gradients, limiting efficiency and convergence during large language model pre-training. TEON addresses this by removing redundant directions across the full gradient tensor structure.
method: Represent gradients/momentum across layers, heads, and parameters as a higher-order tensor to capture multi-mode structure.
Perform orthonormalization along tensor modes (tensorized orthonormalization) to remove redundant directions jointly across layers rather than independently per layer.
Provide a scalable, practical algorithm with improved theoretical convergence guarantees compared to layer-wise Muon (plus implementation choices for efficiency in LLM pre-training).
impact: TEON can improve stability and convergence speed in large model pre-training by exploiting cross-layer gradient structure, potentially reducing training time and improving optimizer robustness without major architecture changes.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic: layer-wise matrix orthonormalization (Muon) vs. tensorized multi-mode orthonormalization (TEON).

paper_title: TEON: Tensorized Orthonormalization Beyond Layer-Wise Muon for Large Language Model Pre-Training
paper_authors: Ruijie Zhang, Yequan Zhao, Ziyue Liu, Zhengyang Wang, Dongyang Li
